quotes.quote: Seed1.8 Model Card: Towards Generalized Real-World Agency
[Submitted on 21 Mar 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 17 Apr 2026 (this version, v3)]
BIOBench is an internal multimodal benchmark designed to evaluate Olympic-level biology knowledge.
The dataset consists of 150 high-difficulty questions, split into 80% multimodal and 20% text-only tasks.
To ensure data quality, every question undergoes rigorous annotation and review by domain experts, guaranteeing accuracy and preventing data contamination.
Here we show one specific example of biology research task from our internal BIOBench.
Based on the advanced vision and reasoning capabilities, Seed1.8 can solve complex scientific problems directly from visual inputs.
Based on these experimental results, which part of the Caspase-5 structure can be omitted during the modification? Among the four modifications, which one is the least effective?
The figure shows several important proteins and their cleaved forms detected by immunoblotting (Western blot).

In this section, we report a comprehensive evaluation of Seed1.8 across three categories.

First, we summarize fundamental LLM capabilities—reasoning, complex instruction following, and knowledge—together with several internal benchmarks intended to approximate high-value application patterns (Table 1).
In section 2.1, section 2.2, and section 2.3 we report the scores of Seed1.8 using think-high.

While established academic benchmarks remain informative for measuring core competencies (e.g., reasoning, knowledge, and instruction following), real-world deployment also depends on multimodal perception, tool use, and end-to-end task completion under latency and interaction constraints.
We compare the results with GPT-5-high, Claude-Sonnet-4.5, Gemini-2.5-pro and Gemini-3-pro.
Furthermore, we build internal benchmarks designed to mirror high-value real-world applications and demonstrate the economic utility of Seed1.8.
